NOTE ON FORM. ab_compare's machine-readable slots are per-capture and a soak produces no captures, so the registered expect_counts below are degenerate on purpose (better=0, worse=0, and must_not_move '*' -- if ANY capture shows up in either arm the request was mis-dispatched as a suites run and every leg here is void). The legs are numbers read off the hakuX-perf logcat line by hand; they are bound here by this file's content hash, which is the point of registering before the device runs.

#54: how often does a device-thread read of guest VRAM race a guest write? Read-side-only instrument, measured on a SOAK (no goldens, so every leg below is read off the logcat by hand from the hakuX-perf pacing line).

THE INSTRUMENT. Two device-thread reads of d->vram_ptr are bracketed, each one preceded by a test-and-CLEAR of the very dirty bits it then scans, which is what turns "written at some point since boot" into a WINDOW:
  Vr:raced/copies     -- sync_vertex_ram_buffer test-and-clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a range and then copies it out of guest memory. The range is clean on entry by construction; a bit set again when the copy returns is a guest store into it DURING the copy.
  Tr:raced/uploads/binds -- pgraph_vk_bind_textures -> check_texture_dirty test-and-clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX and bumps r->texture_vram_gen whenever it finds anything. A gen bump across the bind proves the bits were consumed inside the window; a bit set again on return is a guest store during the upload.
  Tl:                 -- dirty on return with nothing consumed inside the window.
  Xd:                 -- the impossible row, leg 1.
There is no write side, deliberately: a per-page last-written stamp would be a store in every guest VRAM write, which is where the +34.1% instrumentation sat.

ARMS. A = 13ccda425a (the integration branch HEAD, no probe). B = ae0283fe2d (A plus the probe, nothing else). Title and device are held fixed: Dead or Alive 3 on the THOR for the cost pair, whose attract loop renders real gameplay without needing input injection, and Crimson Skies on the THOR as a second reading because its attract FMV is per-frame dynamic VRAM traffic -- the workload #54 itself names as the one the test corpus cannot exercise. One --who across all of them so device_label cannot drift, which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.

LEG 1 -- THE IMPOSSIBLE ROW. Xd reads EXACTLY 0 on every run of arm B.
Xd counts a dirty bit observed to go from set to clear between two back-to-back scans of the same range with nothing between them but the probe's own arithmetic. The guest only ever SETS these bits, and the only code in this process that clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A or _NV2A_TEX is the vertex sync and check_texture_dirty, both on the thread already inside the call. The arithmetic forbids it.
The worlds in which it FAILS, and none of them is forced by the patch: page indices that straddle a DIRTY_MEMORY_BLOCK_SIZE boundary wrongly, so the second scan reads a different word than the first; an RCU blocks pointer that is not stable across the scan; or the pfifo and pgraph.vk.render threads running these paths concurrently after all -- render_thread.c's RCMD_FLUSH does call pgraph_vk_update_vertex_ram_buffer, and this probe assumes the requester waits on flush_complete. A non-zero Xd indicts the instrument, not the emulator, and every other leg below is void until it is explained.

LEG 2 -- THE PATH IS LIVE. tex_binds > 0 AND vtx_copies > 0 on every run of arm B.
A zero denominator means the probe is sitting on a path the device does not take, which is the failure that once made a patch measure 0 better and 0 worse. Fails if either denominator is zero; then the reading is "not measured", never "zero races".

LEG 3 -- THE RATE, which is the measurement #54 needs.
Predicted: 1e-4 <= Tr/tex_uploads <= 3e-1 on Dead or Alive 3.
Not fitted from anything this arm produces. The lower bound is a claim that the window is hit at all in a game; the upper is set by #44, where the same race in a synthetic tight loop loses on 1 to 3 of 12 testifying swatches per run over 6 of 10 runs -- order 10% per upload under maximal pressure -- and a game re-binds far more textures than it re-uploads, so the game rate must sit below that.
The two decisive outcomes, declared before the number exists:
  Tr/tex_uploads effectively zero (< 1e-4, and Tr == 0 on every run) -> the window is never hit in practice, the hazard is theoretical, and #54 CLOSES on evidence rather than on argument. This is the outcome #54's own text predicts under "incidental ordering elsewhere -- locks, syscalls, the PFIFO path itself -- may serialise enough in practice that the window is never hit."
  Tr/tex_uploads >= 1e-4 -> #54 gains a frequency, a call-site list and a target. It does NOT gain a licence for the blanket barrier: the +34.1% experiment already localised that cost to TCG code generation (renderer idle 27 -> 44 ms while frame time went 52 -> 70 ms), so the answer is targeted fences at the few sites a device thread reads guest memory.
The failing world: the guest genuinely never writes a bound texture's page while the upload is reading it, because the pushbuffer handshake serialises them. Real, and nothing in this patch forces it either way -- the probe reads a bitmap the memory subsystem maintains whether the probe exists or not.

LEG 4 -- THE TEXTURE SITE RACES MORE THAN THE VERTEX SITE.
Predicted: Vr/vtx_copies < Tr/tex_uploads.
Mechanism: the vertex window is a memcpy of a few KB; the texture window is a convert, a swizzle and a staging copy of up to megabytes -- one to three orders of magnitude longer, and a race rate scales with the window.
The failing world is concrete rather than rhetorical: a title streaming dynamic vertex buffers rewrites them immediately before drawing from them far more often than it rewrites textures, which inverts the ordering. If it inverts, the target list for a narrow fix changes, and that is a finding rather than a refutation of the instrument.

LEG 5 -- WHETHER THE SAME INSTRUMENT MEASURES #44's SKEW.
Tr counts exactly "the texture's dirty bits were consumed inside the bind window and set again by the time it returned", which is the guest writing the texture while the upload read it -- #44's resolved mechanism, the upload for draw N reading guest memory after the guest has begun writing iteration N+1 to the same address.
Predicted: Tr > 0 on at least one of the arm-B runs.
Stated in advance as the limit, so it is not read into the result later: Tr is a FLOOR on #44's skew rate and cannot be anything else. If the guest completes iteration N+1's write BEFORE check_texture_dirty clears the bits, the clear consumes that write, the upload reads a fully-written successor, and nothing is set again -- #44's `cut == complete` case, which is invisible here. Page granularity (4 KiB) cuts the other way: a write to the same page but a different byte counts, so Tr is an UPPER bound on byte-level overlap. It is a floor on version skew and a ceiling on byte overlap, and those are different quantities.
This lane does not touch pacing. nv2a.c and pfifo.c belong to the skew lane; any overlap is reported to it.

LEG 6 -- COST, with the statistic fixed before the numbers exist.
On this queue a MEDIAN gfps is a measurement of how busy the device is, not of how fast the build is: the series is bimodal (ceiling 29-31, floor 5-20) and the median tracks occupancy, which moved 80% -> 16-32% across one evening. So the cost statistic is ceiling-side and declared here:
  primary   p90 of gfps over all hakuX-perf lines in a soak, and p10 of the G: game frame ms on the same lines.
  reported but NOT a cost read: median gfps, labelled as occupancy.
  noise floor MEASURED, not assumed: two runs per arm, same ref, same title, same device; the floor is the within-arm spread of each statistic.
  decision rule: the probe's cost is "below the noise floor" if |delta p90 gfps| <= max(within-arm spread of the two arms) AND |delta p10 G| <= the same. Anything larger is reported as the cost, in percent, with both arms' spreads printed beside it.
Expected: below the noise floor. The probe adds, per instrumented read, one RCU read-lock and a find_next_bit over at most a handful of machine words -- a 1 MB texture is 256 pages, four longs -- and the second scan behind the impossible row fires only on the rare dirty path. But "read-only" is a claim about a bitmap's implementation and not a measurement, which is why this leg exists.

CONTROLS, not legs.
  mb_emitted must read 0 on the hakuX-build line in BOTH arms. Neither arm restores barriers; a non-zero value means the wrong ref was built.
  Tq: (tex_dirty_queries) must be indistinguishable between the arms. The probe adds no test-and-clear and removes none, so if Tq moves, the probe has changed the path it is observing.
  device_label must read "thor" on all five results. Four soaks across two handhelds with nothing recording which is how #64's cost leg lost its control.

ASSERTIONS, recorded so they are not counted as falsifiers, because the code forces them: Tr <= tex_uploads <= tex_binds, and Vr <= vtx_copies.

WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT DECIDE. Whether a race the probe counts actually corrupted a frame. It counts windows, not wrong pixels, and a soak has no frame capture -- that exclusion is already established on #54 and this instrument does not lift it. It also cannot see the surface-upload read, which is deliberately uninstrumented: nothing on the device clears DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A over a surface range, so the bitmap is monotone there and a probe on it would report a plausible number with no time base in it.
